title: Finite projective nodal towers with finite nonsmooth complements
statement: Let $f:C\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. A projective nodal curve with finite nonsmooth complement is an H-projective [def-kun-projective], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphism with geometrically connected fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], such that for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and every $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$, the geometric fibre $C_s=C\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre] has pure dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension], and every point of $C_s$ either has an open neighbourhood smooth over $\Omega$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] or has completed local ring isomorphic to $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. The completion is the maximal-ideal-adic completion of the stalk [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The relative smooth locus is the union of the opens of $C$ smooth over $S$. Its closed complement has a closed subscheme structure [def-weil-closed-immersion] finite over $S$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. A finite projective nodal tower is an isomorphism (length zero) or a composite $P\to T\to S$ of such a projective nodal curve $P\to T$ and a finite projective nodal tower $T\to S$.
